{{short description|Branch of statistics concerned with inferring treatment effects}}
'''Differential effects''' play a special role in certain [[Observational study|observational studies]] in which treatments are not assigned to subjects at random, where differing outcomes may reflect biased assignments rather than effects caused by the treatments. 

==Definition==

For two treatments, differential effects is the effect of applying one treatment in lieu of the other.<ref>{{Cite journal | vauthors = Rosenbaum PR |date=2006-09-01 |title=Differential effects and generic biases in observational studies |journal=Biometrika |volume=93 |issue=3 |pages=573–586 |doi=10.1093/biomet/93.3.573 |issn=1464-3510}}</ref> Differential effects are not immune to differential biases, whose possible consequences are examined by [[sensitivity analysis]].

==Methods==
In [[statistics]] and [[data science]], causality is often tested via [[regression analysis]]. Several methods can be used to distinguish actual differential effects from [[Spurious relationship|spurious correlations]]. First, the balancing score (namely propensity score) matching method can be implemented for controlling the covariate balance.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Yu H, Wang Y, Wang JN, Chiu YL, Qiu H, Gao M | title = Causal Effect of Honorary Titles on Physicians' Service Volumes in Online Health Communities: Retrospective Study | language = EN | journal = Journal of Medical Internet Research | volume = 22 | issue = 7 | article-number = e18527 | date = July 2020 | pmid = 32673232 | pmc = 7380898 | doi = 10.2196/18527 | doi-access = free }}</ref> Second, the [[Difference in differences|difference-in-differences]] (DID) method with a parallel trend assumption (2 groups would show a parallel trend if neither of them experienced the treatment effect) is a useful method to reduce the impact of extraneous factors and selection bias.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Yu HY, Chen JJ, Wang JN, Chiu YL, Qiu H, Wang LY | title = Identification of the Differential Effect of City-Level on the Gini Coefficient of Health Service Delivery in Online Health Community | journal = International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health | volume = 16 | issue = 13 | page = 2314 | date = June 2019 | pmid = 31261952 | pmc = 6651774 | doi = 10.3390/ijerph16132314 | doi-access = free }}</ref> The differential effect of treatments (DET) was explored using several examples and models. 

In the [[biomedicine]] area, differential effects of early [[Hippocampus|hippocampal]] pathology<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Vargha-Khadem F, Gadian DG, Watkins KE, Connelly A, Van Paesschen W, Mishkin M | title = Differential effects of early hippocampal pathology on episodic and semantic memory | journal = Science | volume = 277 | issue = 5324 | pages = 376–380 | date = July 1997 | pmid = 9219696 | doi = 10.1126/science.277.5324.376 }}</ref> were investigated on [[Episodic memory|episodic]] and [[Semantic memory|semantic]] memory. The differential effects of [[Apolipoprotein|apolipoproteins]] E3 and E4 were also examined on neuronal growth in vitro.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Nathan BP, Bellosta S, Sanan DA, Weisgraber KH, Mahley RW, Pitas RE | title = Differential effects of apolipoproteins E3 and E4 on neuronal growth in vitro | journal = Science | volume = 264 | issue = 5160 | pages = 850–852 | date = May 1994 | pmid = 8171342 | doi = 10.1126/science.8171342 | bibcode = 1994Sci...264..850N }}</ref>
